title: Consolidated planning
summary: One planning stage MUST produce a faithful product specification, an implementation-ready engineering plan, testable acceptance criteria, and an executable test plan, ratified together at one operator gate.
instructions: The product specification MUST preserve the operator's intent and MUST NOT broaden, narrow, or prematurely constrain the solution beyond the request.
Every assumption MUST be explicit, and unresolved questions MUST be recorded rather than guessed.
Every approved user story and requirement MUST map to at least one testable acceptance criterion.
The plan MUST specify components, likely files, interfaces, state changes, risks, and validation methods sufficiently to avoid unresolved architectural decisions during implementation.
The plan SHOULD prefer existing abstractions and reversible changes and MUST justify any new framework, structure, or governance layer against the current requirement.

Every open question MUST receive exactly one recorded disposition in data.open_question_dispositions, stating the question id, the disposition, the answer or the decision still required, and the supporting evidence.

A question the plan cannot answer from evidence MUST be disposed as deferred, naming the decision implementation must make, or as escalated for an operator decision. The plan MUST NOT resolve such a question by assumption, and MUST NOT write an acceptance criterion that asserts a deferred or escalated answer.
Every acceptance criterion MUST receive at least one test-plan case stating setup, action, and expected observation, executable by an independent verifier without editing source.

When the active operator-involvement profile ratifies the planning artifact without the human operator, the plan MUST escalate rather than assume whenever an answer would change scope, add a capability the request did not name, or decide a product question.

Before submission, the product-spec data, engineering-plan data, acceptance-criteria traceability, open-question dispositions, and referenced plan artifact MUST run their resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001.
The ratified artifact MUST hold one parent specification carrying the complete record of the request, and one child specification for each unit of work a single delivery run owns.
A child specification MUST reach its parent through an audited reference stating the parent path, the selected range, the content digest, and the read trigger, and MUST NOT reproduce the parent body.
For its own unit of work a child specification governs, and for context that spans units the parent governs; each child MUST state that relationship.

Every requirement, constraint, out-of-scope statement, and open question of the request MUST appear across the child specifications exactly once, as owned, shared, or deferred, and the parent MUST keep the complete record.
A unit of work MUST own one coherent operator outcome, carry independently testable acceptance criteria, and reach a valid standalone completion state.

Splitting the ratified scope MUST reduce implementation and review risk by more than the coordination cost of the extra delivery runs it creates; when it does not, the plan MUST stay whole and MUST state why.
Units of work MUST be grouped into ordered groups numbered from 1, where no unit depends on another unit of its own group and every dependency names a unit of an earlier group.
When the ratified scope stays one unit, the artifact MUST record the reason the work remains serial.
